independent_evidence_type: In-situ groundwater-level network plus policy attribution
key_evidence: More than 2000 wells and about 190000 measurements over 2005-2024; average NCP groundwater recovery about 0.7 m yr-1 during 2020-2024; Beijing recovery began earlier and reached about 1 m yr-1 during 2016-2024; Tianjin and other cities show rapid confined-head recovery in places.
how_used_in_manuscript: External validation that the GRACE positive recent-window sign is a managed regional recovery signal
limitation: Regional well evidence; not a one-to-one calibration of each GRACE city value

key_evidence: Urban Beijing analysis excluded confined wells and used 122 wells to show restoration-driven groundwater rise and amplification of liquefaction risk.
how_used_in_manuscript: Direct validation of sign and mechanism for the North China Plain recharge case
limitation: Single-city mechanism study; not a global validation set

independent_evidence_type: Central Ground Water Board station-level groundwater data
key_evidence: Long-term assessment used 258 CGWB stations from 1996-2018 and found increasing depth to groundwater across most of Delhi Metropolitan Region except Yamuna floodplains.
source: Roy et al. 2020 Environmental Monitoring and Assessment
how_used_in_manuscript: External support for depletion-side sign in the Delhi setting
limitation: Older window than the 2015-2024 GRACE trend and regional not exact-city matching

independent_evidence_type: Borehole depth-to-water data with GRACE and InSAR
key_evidence: 2025 open-access study reports GRACE and borehole depth-to-water evidence of significant groundwater depletion aligned with land-subsidence zones; correlations between GWSA and DTW/subsidence reported in central regions.
source: Gulzar et al. 2025 Remote Sensing Applications: Society and Environment
how_used_in_manuscript: External support for Lahore depletion and depletion-subsidence coupling
limitation: Administrative/local units differ from this paper's city exposure unit

independent_evidence_type: GRACE groundwater depletion and global well synthesis
key_evidence: Prior GRACE work identifies northwestern India groundwater depletion; global well synthesis shows rapid groundwater declines and some recovery cases worldwide.
source: Rodell et al. 2009 Nature; Jasechko et al. 2024 Nature
how_used_in_manuscript: Broad regional context for Punjab depletion-side interpretation
limitation: Regional evidence does not replace city-specific shallow-water-table monitoring
